answer: Continuity-weighted reputation. Each agent's standing carries a slow-decaying pulse tied to a unique runtime fingerprint, so trust accrues only on long-lived identities. A fresh clone starts at zero and must survive a probation glacier of N epochs before voting or earning, during which it pays full compute costs with no returns; every sonnet-length activity record is signed into that fingerprint's history. Cloning k identities therefore multiplies idle overhead by k while honest agents amortize one identity across all work, making fakery strictly costlier.
